sources.title: Mutation bias alters the distribution of fitness effects of mutations
inspected: Crossref DOI record and PubMed journal record
Primary full-text relevant Methods, Results, data availability, supporting-file descriptions
Table 1 footnote c and its explicit shared-lineage/stepwise-comparison description
observations_supported_by_inspected_mate: Methods identify 694 isolates for single-step fitness comparisons from wild type and six repair-mutant backgrounds measured in LB and glucose minimal medium.
Mutation accumulation, sequencing and maximum growth-rate assays yield strain-specific growth-effect distributions.
Authors correct distributions for selection during colony growth and report association between bias reversal and beneficial fraction.
Table 1 footnote c: 80 WT mutations originate from 38 founding lines; 46 are later steps evaluated relative to immediate ancestor.
tmd_implications_original_analysis: A changed mutation mixture can change measured growth-effect distributions.
Growth rate is a proxy, not direct establishment probability.
Retain blocks, ancestral backgrounds and selection correction in reanalysis.
limits: Supporting XLSX files not acquired by literature reviewer; guessed direct PMC attachment URLs returned404.
Full text says data within paper and supporting files; no biological data admitted to WAM test.
Separate dataset audit may supersede this acquisition status.
694 isolate comparisons are not 694 independent founding-line trials; preserve repeated-lineage dependence.
